core.title: Declare every documentation path the change touches, by exact path
core.given: A plan's work has a recorded documentation declaration, and the convention core supplies its change set.
core.then: Every added, modified or deleted path in the authored documentation tree exactly equals some declared documentation artifact's `path` or some declared removal artifact's `from`.
prefer: Declare exact paths at RATIFY, before the work begins.
To remove a document, declare a removal artifact whose `from` is the removed path. Removing a document is a documentation change.
If an unplanned change IS a documentation change, the declaration was wrong at RATIFY. Re-ratify.
avoid: Widening the declaration to absorb a change that is not a documentation change, such as a typo fix in a rendered artefact or a path you did not mean to touch. Do not touch the documentation tree instead.
Relying on a prefix or glob to cover files. Coverage is exact-path only.
unless: Paths in generated documentation output never need to be declared. They are generated output: a rendered site changing is a consequence of an authored change, and requiring it would make every declaration carry generated paths.
No declaration is recorded at all. That case belongs to the core declaration check, not to this rule.
core.why: Deciding whether a change SHOULD have been declared is semantic and cannot be done deterministically. Detecting that a work with a recorded documentation declaration touched the documentation tree without declaring it can be, and it catches the same drift from the other side. The core check verifies that declared paths were touched, and this part verifies that touched paths were declared. Neither check closes the loop alone.
evidence: Every added, modified or deleted change-set path in the authored documentation tree but not in generated documentation output exactly equals some declared artifact's `path` or some declared removal artifact's `from`.
Deleted documentation paths are checked too. The declaration form for a removal is a removal artifact whose `from` is the deleted path.
Each undeclared documentation change is reported as a violation.
verification: Input: the change set of added, modified or deleted paths under evaluation, handed over by the convention core. The check reads it and never computes it.
Covered means the changed path is string-equal to some declared artifact's `path`, or to the `from` of a declared removal artifact. Prefix and glob matches do not count.
Scope: paths in the authored documentation tree (profile: roots.docs), excluding generated documentation output (profile: roots.docs_generated). Deleted paths are in scope.
If no documentation declaration is recorded, defer to the core declaration check. This rule fires only when a declaration exists and does not cover the change set.
The check needs knowledge of the documentation tree: which root is authored documentation and which subtree beneath it is generated output. The structure profile supplies this knowledge.
Strict disposition, severity 2: every undeclared documentation change is a violation; there is no advisory mode and no ratchet baseline.
Generated documentation output is excluded because it is build output: a rendered-site change is a consequence of an authored change, not an authored change.

fires: A documentation declaration is recorded. The change set modifies a path in the authored documentation tree. No declared artifact's `path` equals it, and no declared removal artifact's `from` equals it either.

A documentation declaration is recorded. The change set deletes a path in the authored documentation tree. No declared artifact's `path` equals it, and no declared removal artifact's `from` equals it either.

A declaration is recorded and one artifact declares only a directory prefix. The change set adds a file beneath that prefix. No declared artifact's `path` or removal `from` exactly equals the added path, so the path is undeclared because coverage is exact-path.
doesNotFire: The only changed documentation paths are in generated documentation output, which is generated build output.
No documentation declaration is recorded at all. That is the core declaration check's concern.
An empty change set is supplied. Nothing changed, so the result permits.
Every changed documentation path outside generated output exactly equals some declared artifact's `path` or some declared removal artifact's `from`.
All changed paths are outside the documentation tree.
No change set is supplied at all. The sibling part that handles the absent-change-set case owns this case.

profileRequirements.meaning: The root of the authored documentation tree whose added, modified and deleted paths must each be exactly declared.
The generated documentation output subtree beneath the documentation root that is never required to be declared, because it is a consequence of authored changes.

proposedKeys.meaning: Root of authored documentation in the repository: the tree whose changed paths a documentation declaration must cover exactly.
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: The roots group covers config, source, test, e2e, plan, scan and the single stack-wide excluded list; none says where authored documentation lives, and documentation is not one of the parametric roles in roles.<role>.

proposedKeys.meaning: Generated documentation output beneath roots.docs: build output that is a consequence of authored changes and is never required to be declared.
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: roots.excluded is the one stack-wide never-scanned list for checkers that defer classification, but this rule states its own in-scope exclusion (the documentation tree IS scanned; only the generated subtree beneath it is exempt), so the exclusion is documentation-tree knowledge rather than the stack-wide list.

bunOnly.text: The rule lives in the docs extension, not in core, because it requires knowing the docs/ tree (spec 2 §4; companion §4, *Deliberately excluded*). Implemented by the validator docs_capability.
bunOnly.reason: Placement of the rule inside the realization's extension, the spec/companion section citations and the validator id (docs_capability) are realization details; the neutral core states generically that the check needs documentation-tree knowledge, which the structure profile supplies.

neutralityNotes: The documentation-declaration schema (documentation, artifacts, action, path, archive/from) and the process terms (change set, RATIFY, the core/capability split) are ATDD-convention vocabulary rather than stack facts, so they stay in the core; a realization whose plan artifact shapes differ maps these fields. Two facts about the documentation tree had no closed-vocabulary key, so roots.docs and roots.docs_generated are proposed; roots.excluded was deliberately not used because the Bun text scopes its own exclusion instead of deferring to a stack-wide list. The Bun fact type 'path_glob' is outside the closed fact vocabulary and was remapped to file_kind with role-level values. Concrete worked examples (the declaration block, the placeholder docs/a.adoc paths in fires) are not repeated in the core; bun.json remains the reference example. Spec and companion section citations were dropped from the core text as convention-document references that add no obligation; the validator id (docs_capability) and the extension-vs-core placement are kept as bunOnly. Per policy, severity 2 and the strict disposition live in core verification rather than the profile.
